implementation_notes: The native C++ form. Capture lists make the dependencies explicit at the definition site, so unlike a JavaScript closure you can read what a lambda depends on without executing it. Supports init-capture for move-in and mutable state for private counters.
idiom_name: lambda expression with an explicit capture list
code_sketch: auto f = [threshold, &cache](int x) { return x > threshold ? cache.hit() : false; };
pitfalls: Reference capture outliving the scope is UB.

variants.name: Function objects via operator()
variants.implementation_notes: Before C++11 the closure is a small class holding the captured values as members and an operator() that uses them. Still the right form when the value must be stored in a container, serialised, compared by identity, or is created once and called many times - a lambda in a std::function allocates exactly like any other.
pitfalls: A functor with virtual operator() or a large member set is allocated per copy into a std::function.
